newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU clears $113 million aid to former Yugoslavia.
newsitem.headline: EU clears $113 million aid to former Yugoslavia.

text.p: The European Commission has cleared a package of humanitarian aid worth $113 million to the former Yugoslavia, the EU executive said in a statement on Thursday.
Aid is intended to help vulnerable groups in the war-affected region, as well as boosting efforts to help the return and reintegration of displaced people and refugees.
"This includes emergency repairs to schools, health centres, houses and infrastructure, especially electricity and water supplies," the statement said.
"This decision should bring benefits to some two million people, 1.3 million of them in Bosnia and Herzegovina, including an expected 200,000 refugees returning from abroad," it added.

Previous humanitarian aid in the former Yugoslavia since fighting began in 1992 totals 1,367 million European currency units ($1,572 million). The statement gave no country-by-country breakdown of the aid. ($=0.87 ecus)
